narrative: The model estimated a 90% probability that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt, and that high predicted risk is why your law school application was denied. The most influential factor was your third-year class-standing decile: you were in decile 1, compared with an average of about 5.8 among accepted students. That much lower standing pushed the prediction strongly toward failure. The second most important factor was your first-year class-standing decile: decile 2 versus an accepted average of about 6.0, which also pushed toward failure. Third was your undergraduate GPA of 2.50, below the accepted-student average of 3.23; this reinforced the same direction, though less strongly than your class standing. Together, these academic indicators drove the model’s high failure estimate despite other information in your profile. To proceed, ask the admissions office for specific feedback, find out whether the decision can be appealed, and consider delaying reapplication until you can show stronger academic preparation. Use that time to seek academic support, improve your record through additional coursework or retaking relevant tests if advised, and consult admissions staff about what evidence would most convincingly show you are ready for law school and bar study.
